title: Macronix AN0363 Managing Unexpected NAND Flash Power Loss in Embedded Systems
note: Software handling of interrupted program/erase and metadata recovery; relevant to switched-power image capture/storage.
first_page_excerpt: APPLICATION NOTE Managing Unexpected NAND Flash Power Loss in Embedded Systems P/N: AN-0363 Ver.01, Dec.17, 2014 1 1. Introduction SLC NAND flash is now becoming the main system storage for executable code and data in embedded systems. It is imperative that the system storage design be reliable and be tolerant of any system failures. When choosing NAND flash as t he main system storage, many reliability issues must be considered such as ECC coverage for possible data error bits, block wear leveling to extend the whole system’s longevity, and the ability to recover from unexpected power loss during system operation--especially when storing code and data. This article will focus on handling the power loss issue from a software point of view. It will start by presenting an outline of an ordinary flash management algorithm and show how it manages the whole flash during normal operations and when a power loss occurs. It will examine the possible negative consequences of an unexpected power loss and discuss a recovery technique to return to normal operation. 2. The Flash Management Algorithm Outline Due to the characteristics of NAND flash, flash man agement methods must be implemented to help upper layer software utilize NA ND flash as a reliable storage device. The first method is called the FTL (Flash Translati on Layer), which is basically a logical to physical address mapping scheme. Figure 2-1 shows a Flash Translation Layer Structure.
